How Do You Build Your Character?
🌍 Nationality: training options set your starting stats, fan support sets your starting popularity. Your first gym and coach also depend on your country.
🎂 Age (18-30): Start young and you're raw but grow fast (×1.3). Start older and you're stronger, but after 32 speed and chin start to decline. Retirement is inevitable at 41.
⚖️ Weight class: Lighter weights are fast and durable, heavyweights hit hard but tire quickly.
🥋 Background: The most important choice. It sets your strengths and weaknesses, and therefore how you fight.
📖 Story: Write it yourself or let the game write it.
🎲 Dice: In the last step your stats are rolled. Don't like them? You can reroll twice.
You start your career with 3 points. Every training camp gives 1-3 points (depending on intensity, age, camp location, coach and staff quality). The camp's focus area also improves by +1-3.
Fights give points too: win 2, finish +1, bonus +1, belt +1. Loss and draw 1 point.
📅 A fight cycle (camp + recovery) takes about 90-100 days. You fight 3-4 times a year; every decision matters.
Spend points on any stat you like. Up to 50, +1 costs 1 point; up to 70, 2; up to 85, 3; after that, 4 points.
You can spend them before the weigh-in at the end of camp, after a fight, or in the DEVELOPMENT tab on the Career screen.
1️⃣ Choose an opponent. In the regional stage you choose; in the major promotions the opponent is assigned.
2️⃣ Camp: focus area, game plan, intensity, weight cut and press conference. A game plan that targets the opponent's weakness gives a big advantage in the cage.
3️⃣ Fight: pick a tactic every round. In critical moments (opponent rocked, submission caught) you make quick decisions.
4️⃣ After: bonuses, interview, rankings, contract offers and events between fights.
🏆 The road: Amateur → Regional (CFC, Oktagon) → Major (PFL, ONE, MVP) → DWCS or short notice → UFC belt.
